requirement:
`OutlineContent::outline` exposes the outline of its whole retained file,
including when the content value selects one item. The outline lists the file
root first, followed by its items in source preorder. Full selectors identify
items and their ancestry under {cite}`requirements.sdk.outlines.selector_syntax`.

```rust,ignore
impl OutlineContent {
    pub fn outline(&self) -> &Outline;
}
```

Each span uses byte offsets into the supplied source snapshot, with an exclusive
end and boundaries valid for slicing that text. It includes the item's attached
source under the language's rules. The root has an empty selector and span
`0..source.len()`.
rationale:
I judged the marked tests adequate for `requirements.sdk.outlines.items`. All of them are in `crates/trust-but-verify/tests/outline_content.rs`. I did not read implementation source.

**Obligations and the tests that cover them**

1. **`outline()` exposes the whole retained file's outline, even when the content value selects one item.**
   - `selected_contents_outlive_handles_and_later_file_edits` builds a selected content from `OutlineContent::from_id` on a non-root selector. It asserts `selected.outline().items.len() == 3`, which is the full file outline of a root plus two lines. It also asserts that `selected.select("")` still returns the retained root text.
   - `markdown_heading_levels_resolve_encoded_duplicates_and_anonymous_items` asserts `std::ptr::eq(second.outline(), contents.outline())` for a selected section.
   - `rust_items_attach_documentation_and_preserve_structural_hashes` asserts the same pointer equality for a selected function.
   - Together these show that a selected value shares the whole-file outline.

2. **The root comes first, then items in source preorder.**
   - `rust_items_attach_documentation_and_preserve_structural_hashes` asserts the exact ordered selector list `["", "mod[auth]", "mod[auth]/fn[check]", "mod[auth]/struct[Token]", "fn[last]"]`. Parents precede children, and the later sibling follows the nested subtree.
   - The same test asserts the ordered kinds list.
   - The Markdown test asserts the ordered nested section selectors, including a block item.
   - The plain-text tests assert line order, for example "alpha", "beta", "alpha".

3. **Spans are byte offsets with an exclusive end and boundaries valid for slicing.**
   - `unicode_spans_use_bytes_and_whitespace_only_lines_create_no_items` uses multi-byte text. It asserts the exact spans `[0..source.len(), 0..2, 6..10]` and slices the source with them.
   - The Markdown tests assert `source.get(span).is_some()` for all items, and assert that `&source[item.span]` equals the selected text, including with non-ASCII headings.
   - `bundled_languages_claim_extensions_and_supply_the_same_public_outline` checks `source.get(item.span)` for every item in all bundled languages.

4. **The span includes attached source under the language's rules.**
   - The Rust test asserts that the function span starts at the `/// Check tokens.` doc comment, that the text contains `#[inline]`, and that the span ends at the function end.
   - The Markdown setext and container tests assert that spans start at the original heading text and include the container underline and body.
   - Language-specific attachment rules belong to the refining `requirements.sdk.sources.*` requirements, which these tests also reference.

5. **The root has an empty selector and span `0..source.len()`.**
   - This is asserted in the Rust, Markdown, unicode and plain-text tests.
   - `bundled_languages_claim_extensions_and_supply_the_same_public_outline` asserts it for every bundled language.
   - The empty-source case asserts `0..0`.

6. **Full selectors identify items and their ancestry.** This clause is a `{cite}` of `selector_syntax`, so it needs no separate coverage here. The tests exercise it anyway: nested selectors, `#N` duplicates, encoded names and `@hash` anonymous nodes.

**Gaps**

I found no untested obligation and no assertion that contradicts the text. No `{fixme}` acknowledgments apply.

text: :::{req} items
`OutlineContent::outline` exposes the outline of its whole retained file,
including when the content value selects one item. The outline lists the file
root first, followed by its items in source preorder. Full selectors identify
items and their ancestry under {cite}`requirements.sdk.outlines.selector_syntax`.
```rust,ignore
impl OutlineContent {
pub fn outline(&self) -> &Outline;
Each span uses byte offsets into the supplied source snapshot, with an exclusive
end and boundaries valid for slicing that text. It includes the item's attached
source under the language's rules. The root has an empty selector and span
`0..source.len()`.
:::{req} selector_syntax
An outline selector MUST be a `/`-separated path of segments from the file's
root node to an outline node; the empty selector MUST select the root node. A
named node's segment MUST be `kind[name]`. An anonymous node's segment MUST be
`kind@hash`, where `hash` is the first twelve hexadecimal digits of its identity
hash under {cite}`requirements.references.structural_hash`. Siblings whose
segments would otherwise be identical MUST be disambiguated by `#N`, their
one-based position among those siblings in source order, except `line` nodes:
identical lines are interchangeable, so a `line` selector MUST resolve when any
line with that content exists in the file. In names, `%`, `[`, `]`, `/`, `#`,
`@`, and whitespace MUST be percent-encoded as UTF-8 bytes, so selectors are
reversible. Line numbers MUST NOT form part of a selector.
